**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 00:45
- [USER] User inquired about the name of the polymer created by mixing baking soda and superglue, referring to it as "glutine."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant stated that the polymer created by mixing baking soda and superglue is not known as "glutine" and that mixing the two will not create a polymer.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained that super glue, also known as cyanoacrylate, forms a strong bond when in contact with moisture, while baking soda is an alkali used as a rising agent in baking.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that mixing baking soda and super glue will create a paste without any particular use.
- [USER] User asserted that mixing baking soda and super glue creates a very hard and useful type of plastic and asked for its chemical name.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant reiterated that mixing baking soda and super glue does not create a hard and useful type of plastic and that there is no chemical reaction between the two that would form a polymer or plastic.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant stated that the method is not recommended and does not create a reliable or suitable material for many applications.
- [USER] User claimed that many people use the mixture to repair items or mold objects.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant apologized for any confusion and acknowledged that some people might use the mixture as an adhesive, sealant, or filler for certain applications.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant cautioned that the mixture is not as strong as the original super glue and may not be as durable as other adhesives.
